title:
Mexico Captures a Most Wanted Drug Lord.
South Korea's Education Minister Quits.
Factory Fire Leaves Dozens Missing.
subject: Mexico Captures a Most Wanted Drug Lord. South Korea's Education Minister Quits. Factory Fire Leaves Dozens Missing.
preview_text: A cartel boss caught, an exam scandal resignation, a deadly blaze, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
description: Mexican forces arrest a suspected cartel boss on the FBI's most wanted list, South Korea's education minister resigns and a factory fire hits Indonesia.
contents_extra: A drone strike on a Russian ship near Finland, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Mexico Arrests a Drug Lord From the FBI's Most Wanted List
paragraphs: The BBC reports Mexican special forces arrested Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Friday. He is known as "Chapo Isidro" and was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list. Mexico's defence secretariat said seven suspects and four soldiers were killed. The US is seeking his extradition, the BBC says.

The Guardian reports the raid used help from US intelligence, according to Mexico's defence ministry. Videos showed civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game in Guasave. Cartel members set up flaming roadblocks overnight, the paper says. By Saturday the violence had substantially subsided, and state authorities said the situation was under control.

stories.title: South Korea's Education Minister Resigns Over an AI Cheating Scandal
paragraphs: The BBC reports Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned over an exam cheating scandal. He took responsibility for confusion over last-minute measures against AI-assisted cheating at the Suneung college entrance exam. Officials sent emergency alerts to every phone in the country. President Lee Jae Myung accepted the resignation, the BBC says.

The Guardian reports the scandal began when a top tax exam scorer confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone. Teachers' unions criticised the government response as belated, the paper says. Choi wrote that he could not escape criticism that officials failed to prepare. The ministry earlier said 111 candidates had unauthorised devices, the BBC says.

photo.alt: Pencil on a multiple choice answer sheet, file photo

stories.title: Fire at an Indonesian Candy Factory Leaves Dozens Missing
paragraphs: The BBC reports at least three people were killed and 36 are missing after a factory fire in western Java. The confectionery plant is in Banten province, about 50km west of Jakarta. Rescuers were searching damaged parts of the building on Sunday. Authorities have not yet determined the cause, the BBC says.

The Guardian reports drone footage showed large parts of the factory destroyed, with the roof collapsed in places. A rescue official said four people were injured. Banten's governor said about 60 people were inside when the fire started on Saturday. Relatives gathered near the entrance seeking news, the paper says.

photo.alt: Smoke rising over an industrial area, file photo

deep_dive.title: What a Drone Strike on a Russian Ship Means for Finland
paragraphs: The BBC reports a Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad was hit by a drone attack on Saturday. The Sparta II caught fire in the eastern Gulf of Finland and drifted into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv had yet to comment, the BBC says.

The Guardian reports Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said war is spilling over into Finland's immediate vicinity. He added that Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor. Finland's defence ministry said it informed Nato. It also imposed temporary restrictions in the eastern gulf. Finland joined the alliance in 2023, the paper notes.

CNBC reports the ship is under US sanctions and linked to Russian shipping company Oboronlogistika. That firm provides logistics for Russia's Defence Ministry, according to its website. A Finnish Border Guard official said military materiel on board could not be ruled out. Swedish combat aircraft helped safeguard Finnish territory, Sweden's defence minister said.

Politico reports Russian state news agency Tass said the vessel carried paints and coatings, citing a single unnamed source. Kaliningrad's governor said two drones were involved. Finland said a Russian helicopter violated its airspace for about five minutes. The defence minister said that was possibly linked to the rescue operation.

trivia.question: How many people does Banten's governor say were inside the Indonesian factory when it caught fire?
trivia.explanation: The answer is about 60. The BBC reports Banten Governor Andra Soni said about 60 people were believed to be inside.

World view: India's Congress youth wing warns of more protests at Meta offices, the Guardian reports members clashed with police in Hyderabad on Friday.
Nigeria's young majority has few young candidates before January's vote, the BBC reports about 80% of Nigerians are under 40.
Europe heads into a supercycle of national elections, the Guardian reports Spain holds a snap vote on Nov. 29.
Need to know: COP31 hosts publish a new draft text, the BBC understands the EU sees it as a backward step.
Two tanker incidents are reported near Oman's Khasab, CNBC reports UKMTO said no casualties were reported.
China's summit diplomacy draws new attention, CNBC reports Xi hosted a rare meeting with Trump and Putin in Shenzhen.
Money & markets: Warren Buffett more than quadruples his Thanksgiving gifts, CNBC reports the donations total $5.5 billion.
CoreWeave's debt raises questions about the AI boom, the Guardian reports on its risky datacentre model.
States and Washington clash over prediction markets, CNBC reports the Senate passed a bill on banned contract types.
Future frontiers: Quantum computing's first payoff may come in energy, CNBC reports firms are testing power grid optimization.
AI characters are cloning real creators' videos, the BBC reports experts call the practice reskinning.
Tech outages fuel spending on emergency supplies, CNBC cites exclusive data from Consumer Edge.
The score: Max Verstappen wins a wild Las Vegas Grand Prix, BBC Sport reports the race had 34 lead changes.
Victor Wembanyama scores 50 as San Antonio beat New Orleans, BBC Sport reports the Spurs won 114 to 91.
Carlos Alcaraz will face Alexander Zverev in the ATP Finals title match, BBC Sport reports Alcaraz came back to beat Ben Shelton.
Life & culture: Jeweller Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89, the BBC reports he helped make his family firm a global luxury brand.
Research links Bank of England directors to enslavement in Cuba, the Guardian reports it continued after British abolition.
Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in Palm Springs, the BBC reports the ceremony was held on Saturday.
